subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost interaction token forgeable via hardcoded HMAC derivation key

question: Should Mattermost interaction signing use a durable configured or SecretRef-backed per-account secret, or should callbacks fail closed until operators explicitly configure that secret?
rationale: The source-level vulnerability is real, but the replacement secret model affects security, setup, upgrade behavior, public docs, and valid button delivery after restarts or across processes.

options.title: Require Durable Secret Provisioning
options.body: Use a configured or persisted per-account interaction signing secret with setup, SecretRef/docs, tests, and restart/split-process proof before merge.

options.title: Accept Explicit Fail-Closed Setup
options.body: Require operators to configure an interaction secret and make missing configuration fail closed with clear docs, diagnostics, and tests.

options.title: Pause For Narrow Replacement
options.body: Close or pause the dirty linked branch and sponsor a replacement once the credential model is chosen.

recommendation.title: Require Durable Secret Provisioning
recommendation.body: Use a configured or persisted per-account interaction signing secret with setup, SecretRef/docs, tests, and restart/split-process proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc recently owned adjacent Mattermost interaction callback hardening, which is the closest current-main security-boundary history for this decision.
